A tall vertical 3:5 book-cover image on full-frame warm ivory aged paper, shown as a flat orthographic scan with no border and no mockup. Keep 78%-85% of the canvas as quiet unprinted paper. Place one compact visual cluster in the lower-left quadrant, occupying about 15% of the canvas and staying comfortably away from every edge.

The cluster contains one small torn grayscale photograph of a distant sunset horizon, partly overlapped by one thin translucent rice-paper fragment. Use low-contrast photocopy softness, irregular hand-torn fibers, restrained halftone grain, and slight ink misregistration. Add only one short piece of matte archival tape. Do not add more photographs, stickers, stamps, circles, diagrams, or decorative scraps.

Use almost no typography: only tiny serif/typewriter archive notation reading "45 / AFTER SUNSET" beside the photograph, with generous spacing and no large headline. The single color anchor is one fully saturated burnt-orange risograph sun cutout, occupying about 1.5% of the whole canvas and about 20% of the small cluster. Keep all other ink subdued charcoal and warm gray; retain visible paper fibers and slight old-print wear.

The result feels quiet, poetic, nostalgic, diary-like, and independent-zine editorial. Matte absorbent paper, diffuse even light, flat scanned appearance, low-to-medium contrast. Avoid a dense scrapbook, full-bleed scene, commercial poster hierarchy, large display lettering, handwriting, logos, product advertising, glossy mockups, hard shadows, 3D depth, cinematic lighting, neon, anime, cute cartoons, multiple accent colors, and long text.
